ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Bacillus subtilis can secrete cellulase. Researchers screened a Bacillus subtilis strain (strain B) with relatively strong ability to degrade cellulose, and cloned from it a cellulase (C1 enzyme) gene. The obtained C1 enzyme gene was connected with a high-efficiency expression vector (HT plasmid), and then introduced into strain B, in the hope of obtaining engineered bacteria with stronger ability to degrade cellulose. The C1 enzyme gene uses the B strand as the transcription template strand, and during transcription the extension direction of the mRNA itself is 5'→3'. In order to connect the C1 enzyme gene with the enzyme-cut HT plasmid in the correct direction, restriction sites for Sma I and BamH I were added to its two ends when cloning the C1 enzyme gene. There are no restriction sites for these two enzymes inside this gene. What are the enzymes corresponding to restriction sites 1 and 2 in Figure 1, respectively?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: BamHI, SmaI (the order cannot be exchanged)

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The upper part of Figure 1 shows the C1 enzyme gene, with the left end labeled as restriction site 1 and the right end labeled as restriction site 2; the A strand has 5' at the left end and 3' at the right end, and the B strand has 3' at the left end and 5' at the right end. The lower part of Figure 1 shows the HT plasmid cut open; the left cut is labeled Sma I, and the right cut is labeled BamH I; the promoter is located near the right cut, and the arrow points to the left, indicating transcription is initiated from right to left. Then reason: The stem states that the C1 enzyme gene uses the B strand as the transcription template strand, while RNA polymerase moves along the template strand in the 3'→5' direction, and the synthesized mRNA direction is 5'→3'. In the figure, the promoter drives transcription from right to left, so after insertion, the B strand serving as the template should have 3' at the right end and 5' at the left end. In the original C1 gene, the B strand is 3' at the restriction site 1 end and 5' at the restriction site 2 end, so restriction site 1 should connect to the BamH I end on the right side of the plasmid, and restriction site 2 should connect to the Sma I end on the left side of the plasmid. Therefore, restriction sites 1 and 2 correspond to BamH I and Sma I, respectively.
